title: People, tools and safe work
brief: A fictional community-access project has a 90 m × 4 m work strip. The plan protects a walking route, uses a designated truck guide and requires a working broom dust-control system. At 08:20, the guide’s radio fails and the broom dust-control indicator shows a fault. A draft note says “continue while the guide shouts.” The crew’s shift gap is 11 hours, with 2 hours travel and 2 hours other responsibilities. No safe clearance or operating temperature is supplied.
answer: Area = 360 m². Sleep opportunity = 11 − 2 − 2 = 7 hours, not a fitness-for-work determination. Hold affected movement/work, restore communication and dust controls through the authorized process; revise the draft.
change: The protected walking route must move because an entrance is needed; the responsible lead has not yet approved a new route.
change_answer: Preserve the existing safe controls and obtain an approved revised access plan before dependent movement.

title: Materials, plants and quality evidence
case_title: Trace a material and its sample
brief: A fictional 1,200 g aggregate sample has retained masses of 180 g, 420 g, 360 g and 240 g in the pan. Its log says Mix M, lot 4, but the container label says lot 5. A draft report says “the sample is representative because it is large” and “20% RAP means 20% lower emissions.” The project location is in Metro Vancouver. No acceptance limits or permit number are supplied.
answer: Retained total = 1,200 g; cumulative passing after three sieves = 85%, 50%, 20%. Resolve the lot mismatch; sample size does not establish representativeness. RAP percentage does not establish emission reduction. Confirm the applicable Metro regulatory/permit requirements; do not apply the provincial Asphalt Plant Regulation as if it covered Metro.
change: The quality lead supplies a corrected source record linking the container to lot 5, with documented authorization and preserved original record.
change_answer: Update the traceability record transparently; do not erase the original discrepancy or infer acceptance limits.

title: Road geometry and acceptance
case_title: Check the grade and the quantity
brief: A fictional rectangle is 80 m × 3.5 m. Assigned mix mass is 33.6 t and specified application rate is 120 kg/m². Benchmark EL is 100.000 m, backsight 1.300 m, foresight 1.720 m and target base EL 99.650 m. A draft claims “the application rate proves the whole mat is accepted.” No density or smoothness results are supplied.
answer: Area 280 m²; actual rate 33,600/280 = 120 kg/m², or 100% of specified. HI 101.300; measured EL 99.580; fill 70 mm at that point. Application rate alone does not establish density, smoothness, uniform thickness or acceptance.
change: A corrected drawing changes width to 3.6 m before placement; the mass allocation has not been revised.
change_answer: New area 288 m². The same 33.6 t would give 116.67 kg/m², about 97.22% of 120. Confirm the authorized quantity/layout change before treating it as the current plan.

title: Milling and reclaiming
case_title: Hand over a controlled milling pass
brief: A fictional approved training strip is 60 m × 2 m with a 0.04 m nominal cut. Safe recorded checks at three locations are 40, 41 and 53 mm. The last location follows a disturbed reference. A draft handover states “average depth acceptable; continue.” No project tolerance is supplied. The discharge route remains within a controlled area.
answer: Geometric removed volume = 4.8 m³ in place. Mean of readings = 44.67 mm, but the mean cannot establish conformity or hide the 53 mm reading. Hold the affected work and verify the reference, limits and authorized correction.
change: The next shift uses a different machine model and a different rotor configuration.
change_answer: Reconfirm matching OMM, controls, maintenance and setup; transfer the verified site information without transferring unsupported machine settings.

title: Paver operation
case_title: Keep delivery and mat records consistent
brief: A fictional approved area is 50 m × 3.2 m with a 45 mm compacted target. A verified trial relationship is loose/compacted = 1.24 for this exercise. The delivery register contains ticket 81 for 12 t and ticket 82 for 11 t, but a draft totals 35 t by counting ticket 81 twice. No density for estimating required mass is supplied.
answer: Area 160 m²; compacted geometric volume 7.2 m³; trial-based loose estimate 55.8 mm. Unique delivered tickets total 23 t, not 35 t. Do not infer required mass or acceptance without the missing density/criteria.
change: The coordinator asks for an audio handover as well as an editable table and PDF.
change_answer: Create a checked script from the verified facts, identify the actual narration tool, retain transcript and inspect the audio; keep all file versions consistent.

title: Screed control and handwork
brief: A fictional rectangular repair is 2.5 m × 1.2 m with a 0.05 m compacted depth. The structure elevation and joint treatment are supplied by an approved drawing, but no mixture density or universal compaction allowance is given. A draft proposes heating any cooled mix with a torch and using the same loose-thickness factor on every job.
answer: Area 3.0 m²; compacted volume 0.15 m³. Required mass and loose allowance need appropriate project information. Reject the universal factor and default torch proposal; use the authorized mixture, placement, temperature and heating procedures.
change: The work boundary narrows beside a public entrance and the long lute handle would cross it.
change_answer: Reassess the route, tool orientation and work positions with the lead/TCP team; preserve safe access and brief an approved change before proceeding.

title: Compaction and final handover
case_title: Read the rolling record and its limits
brief: A fictional density record gives in-place 2.325 Mg/m³ and maximum theoretical 2.500 Mg/m³. A coverage sketch marks strips A and B complete and C awaiting a check. A draft says “93% means the whole lot is accepted” and “six passes always work.” No contract limit, sub-lot results or approved fixed pass count is supplied.
answer: Percent density = 93.0% using the stated maximum-theoretical reference. It does not establish whole-lot acceptance. Preserve the pending strip and actual trial/temperature/coverage evidence; reject a universal six-pass claim.
change: The spray system develops a dry stripe and the operator observes material pickup.
change_answer: Report and hold/stop as required, investigate the actual spray/scraper system safely and obtain authorized correction before resuming.
